question: Should OpenClaw accept a generic durable plugin `allowAlwaysKey` API and built-in Skill Workshop opt-in now, or keep `allow-always` persistence plugin-owned until a non-sensitive audited scope is designed?
rationale: Durable plugin approval reuse can suppress future security prompts and becomes a plugin API contract, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent trust boundary or Skill Workshop ownership model.

options.title: Fix scope before merge
options.body: Require a stable core/plugin owner, non-sensitive key material, preserved current-main approval hardening, and second-call reuse proof before this PR can land.

options.title: Split Skill Workshop opt-in
options.body: Land the generic API only after API review and keep Skill Workshop on `allow-once`/`deny` until its lifecycle approval evidence model is ready.

options.title: Pause durable persistence
options.body: Close or pause this branch and route durable approval persistence through the broader owner-approval design discussion before adding core state.

recommendation.title: Fix scope before merge
recommendation.body: Require a stable core/plugin owner, non-sensitive key material, preserved current-main approval hardening, and second-call reuse proof before this PR can land.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision centers on the plugin approval API and durable approval framework that this history most directly owns.
